answer: Network-topology diversity resists Sybil attacks: every identity must periodically answer latency challenges from independent observers across the globe, proving it sits at a distinct point on the network atlas. A fake swarm run from one server shares one latency fingerprint, no matter how many keys it mints. Like jade graded by its veins, each proof is checked against the horizon of known honest nodes, and clones clustering at one vantage point are frozen. An attacker wanting 1000 identities must rent 1000 separate network positions, turning free keys into real infrastructure cost.
